docs.text: HardFOC CI tools ESP-IDF CI Tools ¶ Reusable GitHub Actions workflows for ESP-IDF projects. One builds every example app across a matrix of ESP-IDF versions and build types and reports the firmware size; the other attaches that firmware to a GitHub Release. Quickstart ru-build Source on GitHub Every HardFOC driver, hf-core , hf-internal-interface-wrap and the board HALs build their ESP32 examples with these workflows. A caller writes about fifteen lines of YAML and pins @v1 ; the matrix comes from the caller's own app_config.yml , read by the scripts in hf-espidf-project-tools . C++ lint, documentation and the CI gate live in hf-general-ci-tools . From push to release Figure description and sources From top to bottom. A HardFOC repository calls ru-build from its ESP32 build workflow. ru-build's first job finds hf-espidf-project-tools (a submodule, the project_tools_dir input, or a clone) and turns app_config.yml into a build matrix. The build job runs once per matrix entry inside the espressif/idf Docker image and uploads the build folder as a fw-* artifact. On pull requests the size-report job comments a size table. When the caller pushes a version tag, ru-release-with-artifacts downloads the fw-* artifacts built for that commit and attaches them to a GitHub Release. Job names are read from the workflow files. Drawn from: .github/workflows/ru-build.yml jobs ; .github/workflows/ru-release-with-artifacts.yml jobs ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/workflow-flow.py . What it provides ¶ Workflow or action What it does Caller grants ru-build.yml Builds every app, IDF version and build type in app_config.yml , uploads fw-* artifacts, comments a size table on pull requests contents: read , pull-requests: write ru-release-with-artifacts.yml On a tag, creates a GitHub Release with the fw-* artifacts built for that commit contents: write ensure-tools-directory Composite action: finds or clones hf-espidf-project-tools in your own jobs none What you get ¶ One matrix, one source. The apps, ESP-IDF versions, build types and exclusions are read from app_config.yml , the same file the local build scripts use. See ru-build . Builds that survive Docker Hub. The image is pulled up to four times with back-off before the build. A size table on every pull request , and an optional size budget that fails the run. Releases that ship what was tested. The release attaches the artifacts of the build that ran on the tagged commit; nothing is rebuilt. See ru-release-with-artifacts . A stable contract. @v1 never removes an input or asks for a new permission; the self-CI enforces it. See Versioning and the permissions contract . Where to go next ¶ Quickstart Add the build workflow to a repository with ESP32 examples. ru-build Jobs, inputs, artifacts, size report and failure modes. ru-release-with-artifacts Ship the tested firmware with each version tag. Permissions contract What a caller must grant, and why a missing grant fails at startup.

docs.text: Changelog ¶ What changed in each release of the workflows. A heading Breaking means callers must change before moving to the new major. [Unreleased] ¶ Changed ¶ Documentation moved to the HardFOC MkDocs platform: one page per workflow, inputs tables and the permissions contract generated from the workflow files, published with ru-mkdocs-publish.yml . The README follows the HardFOC README standard; its license badge now names the repository's real license (GPL-3.0). [1.1.0] - 2026-11-02 ¶ Added ¶ Self-CI ( ci-self.yml ): pinned actionlint and shellcheck; shellcheck for the composite actions; a check for run: blocks ending in a bare cond && cmd ; the permissions contract check and the breaking-change check; a check that ru-build's inlined tools-directory step matches the action; unit tests. README permissions table, listing exactly what each caller must grant. release.yml : on a vX.Y.Z tag, creates a GitHub Release with generated notes and moves the vX major tag. Dependabot for GitHub Actions (weekly). Changed ¶ Every third-party action is pinned to a full commit SHA with a version comment. dawidd6/action-download-artifact moves v2 → v28 and softprops/action-gh-release moves v1 → v3.0.3; the old majors used runtimes GitHub no longer supports. Permissions are declared per job. ru-build asks for contents: read and pull-requests: write , and no longer for actions: read . ru-build.yml runs the tools-directory logic inline instead of calling ensure-tools-directory@main . A caller pinned to @v1 therefore runs the v1 copy. The composite action stays available for direct use. Fixed ¶ ru-build.yml size report: "`size.txt missing`" ran a command named size.txt instead of printing the text. [1.0.0] - 2026-11-01 ¶ The first tagged release: the workflows as callers used them from @main . Added ¶ ru-build.yml : the ESP-IDF Docker image is pulled before the build, with up to 4 attempts (10/30/60 s backoff). A transient Docker Hub error no longer fails the build with exit 125. ru-build.yml frees runner disk space before the build.

docs.text: ensure-tools-directory ¶ Find hf-espidf-project-tools in a checkout, or clone it, from a job of your own. File: .github/actions/ensure-tools-directory/action.yml ru-build runs the same script inline: a reusable workflow cannot use an action of its own repository at the caller's ref, so uses: ...@main inside it would run main 's copy for callers pinned to @v1 . The self-CI fails when the two copies differ. Use the action only in jobs you write yourself. Usage ¶ steps : - uses : actions/checkout@v4 with : submodules : recursive - id : tools uses : hardfoc/hf-espidf-ci-tools/.github/actions/ensure-tools-directory@v1 with : project_dir : examples/esp32 - run : python3 "${{ steps.tools.outputs.project_tools_path }}/generate_matrix.py" --validate Inputs and outputs ¶ Input Required Default Description project_tools_dir no - Path to project tools directory (contains scripts directly). Leave empty to auto-detect. project_dir no . Path to the ESP-IDF project (contains CMakeLists.txt) auto_clone_tools no true Auto-clone tools repo if project_tools_dir is missing Output Description project_tools_path Resolved path to the project tools directory The search order is the one on the ru-build page. The action checks that generate_matrix.py , build_app.sh and config_loader.sh exist and makes them executable; it fails with a hint when the folder is missing and cloning is not allowed.

docs.text: Migrating to v1 ¶ Move a caller from @main (or an older copy of these workflows) to the versioned @v1 . Steps ¶ Change the ref in every uses: line: uses : hardfoc/hf-espidf-ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-build.yml@v1 Grant the contract on the calling job: contents: read and pull-requests: write for ru-build , contents: write for ru-release-with-artifacts . ru-build no longer needs actions: read ; you can remove it. Remove callers of workflows that do not exist. Older documentation showed a security.yml reusable workflow; there has never been one in this repository. Use the C++ analysis workflows of hf-general-ci-tools instead. Drop references to the composite action at @main in your own jobs; pin it to @v1 too. Start a new run after the change. "Re-run failed jobs" keeps the old workflow revision. What changed for callers in v1 ¶ Before In v1 Actions pinned to tags, some on runtimes GitHub no longer runs Every action pinned to a commit SHA ru-build asked for actions: read contents: read , pull-requests: write only ru-build called ensure-tools-directory@main The script is inlined, so @v1 runs the v1 copy A Docker Hub error failed the build with exit 125 The image is pulled up to four times first The size report ran a command named size.txt when the file was missing It prints the message No input was removed or made required, so a caller that worked on @main works on @v1 once it grants the permissions above. The full list is in the changelog .

docs.text: Permissions contract ¶ What each workflow needs from its caller, why a missing grant fails before any job starts, and how the contract is kept. What to grant ¶ A called workflow's jobs can use at most the permissions the calling job grants. Grant at least: Workflow Caller must grant Why ru-build.yml contents: read , pull-requests: write checkout; firmware size comment on pull requests ru-release-with-artifacts.yml contents: write create the release and upload the firmware Set them on the calling job, as in the Quickstart . A top-level permissions: block in the caller also works, but then every job in that file gets them. What happens when a grant is missing ¶ GitHub checks the permissions before it starts the called workflow. If a job asks for more than the caller grants, the run ends with startup_failure , shows no jobs and no logs, and only the run summary names the problem. This is why the contract is part of the version: a new permission on @v1 would break every caller at once. How the contract is kept ¶ Every job in a ru-*.yml declares its own permissions: ; a top-level block is not allowed. .github/scripts/check_permissions.py (self-CI) fails when the union of a workflow's job permissions differs from the table above in either direction, when a workflow has no row, or when a caller in this repository grants less. .github/scripts/check_contract.py fails a pull request that widens a permission without a ### Breaking entry in the changelog; that change needs a new major. See Versioning . The table above is the README's, copied when the site is built, so the site and the checked table are the same.

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Add an ESP32 build to a repository in three files: the app list, the tools and a fifteen-line workflow. What the workflow expects ¶ File Purpose examples/esp32/CMakeLists.txt The ESP-IDF project: idf.py build works in this folder examples/esp32/app_config.yml The apps to build, with the ESP-IDF versions, build types and target examples/esp32/scripts/ hf-espidf-project-tools as a submodule (or let the workflow clone it) examples/esp32 is the HardFOC convention and the path the matrix script looks in first; see The matrix before you put the project anywhere else. Add the tools as a submodule: git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-espidf-project-tools.git examples/esp32/scripts List the apps in examples/esp32/app_config.yml : --- metadata : target : esp32c6 idf_versions : [ "release/v5.5" ] build_types : [[ "Debug" , "Release" ]] apps : gpio_test : description : GPIO self-test source_file : GpioTest.cpp Call the workflow from .github/workflows/esp32-examples-build-ci.yml : --- name : ESP32 examples build on : push : branches : [ main ] pull_request : jobs : build : uses : hardfoc/hf-espidf-ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-build.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read pull-requests : write with : project_dir : examples/esp32 project_tools_dir : examples/esp32/scripts Open a pull request. The run shows one job per app, ESP-IDF version and build type, uploads a fw-<app>-<idf>-<build type> artifact for each and comments a size table on the pull request. Grant the permissions in the calling job A reusable workflow cannot use more permissions than its caller grants. Without pull-requests: write the run fails before any job starts ( startup_failure ). See the permissions contract . Add releases ¶ To attach the firmware to a GitHub Release on every v* tag, add .github/workflows/release.yml : --- name : Release on : push : tags : [ "v*" ] jobs : release : uses : hardfoc/hf-espidf-ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-release-with-artifacts.yml@v1 permissions : contents : write with : build_workflow : esp32-examples-build-ci.yml The build must have run on the tagged commit first; see ru-release-with-artifacts . Next: ru-build , every input and what can go wrong.

docs.text: ru-build ¶ Build every ESP32 example app of a repository across ESP-IDF versions and build types, upload the firmware and report its size on pull requests. File: .github/workflows/ru-build.yml Caller ¶ --- name : ESP32 examples build on : push : branches : [ main ] pull_request : workflow_dispatch : inputs : clean_build : type : boolean default : false jobs : build : uses : hardfoc/hf-espidf-ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-build.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read pull-requests : write with : project_dir : examples/esp32 project_tools_dir : examples/esp32/scripts clean_build : ${{ inputs.clean_build || false }} max_dec_total : "0" Inputs ¶ Input Type Required Default Description project_dir string yes - Path to the ESP-IDF project (contains CMakeLists.txt) project_tools_dir string no - Path to project tools directory (contains scripts directly). Leave empty to auto-detect. clean_build boolean no false Skip caches for a clean build. auto_clone_tools boolean no true Auto-clone tools repo if project_tools_dir is missing max_dec_total string no 0 Maximum total dec size in bytes for size budget enforcement (0 to disable) Jobs and permissions ¶ Job Runs Permissions generate-matrix always contents: read build once per matrix entry, fail-fast: false , 30 min limit contents: read size-report pull requests only pull-requests: write generate-matrix checks out with submodules, finds the project tools (below), runs generate_matrix.py and outputs the matrix. build frees runner disk space, checks out, restores the pip cache (skipped with clean_build ), installs the tools' requirements.txt , pulls espressif/idf:<version> (4 attempts, 10 / 30 / 60 s apart), runs build_app.sh inside the image with espressif/esp-idf-ci-action and uploads the build folder. size-report downloads every fw-* artifact, writes a size table from size.info / size.txt , comments it on the pull request and enforces max_dec_total when it is not 0 . The caller grants the union: contents: read and pull-requests: write . See the permissions contract . Finding the project tools ¶ The generate-matrix job needs generate_matrix.py , build_app.sh and config_loader.sh from hf-espidf-project-tools . It looks, in this order: Case Path used project_tools_dir set That path; the job fails if it does not exist (no clone) project_tools_dir empty and <project_dir>/hf-espidf-project-tools exists That folder Otherwise hf-espidf-project-tools at the repository root, cloned from main (depth 1) when it is missing and auto_clone_tools is true A submodule is the reproducible choice: the clone follows the tools' main branch. The matrix ¶ generate_matrix.py reads app_config.yml and emits one entry per app, ESP-IDF version and build type: app_config.yml Effect metadata.idf_versions ESP-IDF branches or tags, for example release/v5.5 ; default release/v5.5 metadata.build_types One list per IDF version, by index: [["Debug", "Release"], ["Debug"]] metadata.target Chip passed to the build, default esp32c6 apps.<name>.idf_versions , apps.<name>.build_types Per-app overrides; a flat build_types list applies to every version apps.<name>.ci_enabled: false Leaves the app out of CI ci_config.exclude_combinations Entries whose keys all match are dropped, for example {app_name: x, build_type: Release} Where app_config.yml is found The workflow runs generate_matrix.py without --project-path , so the script looks for examples/esp32/app_config.yml from the repository root, then for app_config.yml in the folder above the script. Keep the project in examples/esp32 , or keep the tools inside the project folder, so both point at the same file. Artifacts ¶ Each build uploads <project_dir>/build* as fw-<app_name>-<idf_version_docker>-<build_type> , for example fw-gpio_test-release-v5.5-Debug , kept for 7 days. build_app.sh writes size.info and size.txt into the build folder; the size report reads them. The upload runs even when the build fails, so a failed build's logs are in the artifact. Size report and budget ¶ On pull requests the size-report job comments a table with one row per build (app, IDF, target, build type and the idf.py size summary). Set max_dec_total to a byte count to fail the job when any build's total dec size is larger; 0 turns the check off. When it fails ¶ Symptom Cause Fix startup_failure , no job ran The calling job grants less than contents: read , pull-requests: write Add the permissions to the calling job Project tools directory not found project_tools_dir points at a missing folder, or the submodule was not added Add the submodule, or leave project_tools_dir empty to clone Required script ... not found The tools folder is not hf-espidf-project-tools, or is an old copy Update the submodule Configuration file not found No app_config.yml where generate_matrix.py looks (see the warning above) Move the project to examples/esp32 or the tools into the project Could not pull espressif/idf:... after 4 attempts Docker Hub outage, or an IDF version with no image Check the version name; start a new run No build directory found! build_app.sh failed before creating build* Read the build step log; reproduce locally with build_app.sh Size budget exceeded A build's dec total is above max_dec_total Shrink the firmware or raise the budget A fix here does not apply "Re-run failed jobs" reuses the workflow revision of the first run Start a new run (see Versioning ) Next: ru-release-with-artifacts , which ships these artifacts.

docs.text: Job Runs Permissions generate-matrix always contents: read build once per matrix entry, fail-fast: false , 30 min limit contents: read size-report pull requests only pull-requests: write generate-matrix checks out with submodules, finds the project tools (below), runs generate_matrix.py and outputs the matrix. build frees runner disk space, checks out, restores the pip cache (skipped with clean_build ), installs the tools' requirements.txt , pulls espressif/idf:<version> (4 attempts, 10 / 30 / 60 s apart), runs build_app.sh inside the image with espressif/esp-idf-ci-action and uploads the build folder. size-report downloads every fw-* artifact, writes a size table from size.info / size.txt , comments it on the pull request and enforces max_dec_total when it is not 0 . The caller grants the union: contents: read and pull-requests: write . See the permissions contract .
docs.title: Jobs and permissions

docs.text: The generate-matrix job needs generate_matrix.py , build_app.sh and config_loader.sh from hf-espidf-project-tools . It looks, in this order: Case Path used project_tools_dir set That path; the job fails if it does not exist (no clone) project_tools_dir empty and <project_dir>/hf-espidf-project-tools exists That folder Otherwise hf-espidf-project-tools at the repository root, cloned from main (depth 1) when it is missing and auto_clone_tools is true A submodule is the reproducible choice: the clone follows the tools' main branch.
docs.title: Finding the project tools

docs.text: generate_matrix.py reads app_config.yml and emits one entry per app, ESP-IDF version and build type: app_config.yml Effect metadata.idf_versions ESP-IDF branches or tags, for example release/v5.5 ; default release/v5.5 metadata.build_types One list per IDF version, by index: [["Debug", "Release"], ["Debug"]] metadata.target Chip passed to the build, default esp32c6 apps.<name>.idf_versions , apps.<name>.build_types Per-app overrides; a flat build_types list applies to every version apps.<name>.ci_enabled: false Leaves the app out of CI ci_config.exclude_combinations Entries whose keys all match are dropped, for example {app_name: x, build_type: Release} Where app_config.yml is found The workflow runs generate_matrix.py without --project-path , so the script looks for examples/esp32/app_config.yml from the repository root, then for app_config.yml in the folder above the script. Keep the project in examples/esp32 , or keep the tools inside the project folder, so both point at the same file.
docs.title: The matrix

docs.text: Each build uploads <project_dir>/build* as fw-<app_name>-<idf_version_docker>-<build_type> , for example fw-gpio_test-release-v5.5-Debug , kept for 7 days. build_app.sh writes size.info and size.txt into the build folder; the size report reads them. The upload runs even when the build fails, so a failed build's logs are in the artifact.
docs.title: Artifacts

docs.text: On pull requests the size-report job comments a table with one row per build (app, IDF, target, build type and the idf.py size summary). Set max_dec_total to a byte count to fail the job when any build's total dec size is larger; 0 turns the check off.

docs.text: ru-release-with-artifacts ¶ Create a GitHub Release for a tag and attach the firmware that ru-build built and tested for the same commit. File: .github/workflows/ru-release-with-artifacts.yml Caller ¶ --- name : Release on : push : tags : [ "v*" ] jobs : release : uses : hardfoc/hf-espidf-ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-release-with-artifacts.yml@v1 permissions : contents : write with : build_workflow : esp32-examples-build-ci.yml fail_on_no_artifacts : true Inputs ¶ Input Type Required Default Description build_workflow string no esp32-examples-build-ci.yml Name of the ESP32 build workflow artifact_pattern string no fw-.* Pattern for firmware artifacts draft boolean no false Create as draft release prerelease boolean no false Mark as pre-release tag_name string no "" Tag name for release (defaults to github.ref_name) fail_on_no_artifacts boolean no false Fail if no firmware artifacts found Jobs and permissions ¶ One job, release , with contents: write . It checks out with full history, downloads every artifact whose name matches artifact_pattern from the run of build_workflow on github.sha ( dawidd6/action-download-artifact ), and creates the release for tag_name (default: the pushed tag) with generated notes and the files attached ( softprops/action-gh-release ). The workflow does not ask for actions: read : existing callers grant only contents: write , and the token can read artifacts of its own repository without it. When it finds no firmware ¶ The release only reuses artifacts; it never builds. It finds none when: the build workflow has not run on the tagged commit (tag a commit that was pushed to a branch the build runs on, and wait for that build to finish); the artifacts expired ( ru-build keeps them 7 days); build_workflow names a different file than the caller of ru-build ; artifact_pattern (a regular expression, default fw-.* ) does not match. With fail_on_no_artifacts: false (the default) the release is still created, without firmware, and the step logs a warning. Set it to true to fail instead. When it fails ¶ Symptom Cause Fix startup_failure The calling job does not grant contents: write Grant it in the calling job Resource not accessible by integration when creating the release The repository restricts the workflow token to read Grant contents: write in the caller; check Settings > Actions > Workflow permissions Release has no files See above Set fail_on_no_artifacts: true to catch it Next: ensure-tools-directory , for your own jobs that need the project tools.

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How this repository checks its own workflows on every pull request, and how callers gate on them. Self-CI ¶ ci-self.yml runs on every pull request, on any base branch: Check Fails on actionlint with shellcheck (pinned versions, SHA-256 verified) Any finding in a workflow, including shell in run: blocks shellcheck_actions.py Any shellcheck finding in a composite action check_run_tails.py A run: block that ends in a bare cond && cmd , which fails the step when cond is false check_permissions.py A job permission that differs from the permissions contract gen_readme_inputs.py --check A README inputs table that no longer matches its workflow Inlined tools step ru-build 's tools-directory script differing from the composite action check_contract.py A removed input, a new required input, a changed type or a wider permission without a ### Breaking changelog entry test_checks.py The check scripts themselves Run the Python checks locally: pip install 'PyYAML==6.0.2' python .github/scripts/check_permissions.py python .github/scripts/gen_readme_inputs.py --check python .github/scripts/test_checks.py Documentation and text ¶ Workflow Checks ci-docs-publish.yml Strict site build, generated tables and figure drift, link check, Lighthouse; publishes on main ci-markdown-lint.yml , ci-yaml-lint.yml , ci-docs-linkcheck.yml Markdown style, YAML style, links in the repository's Markdown These call the versioned workflows of hf-general-ci-tools . After editing a workflow's inputs, refresh both copies of its table: python .github/scripts/gen_readme_inputs.py # README.md hardfoc-docs gen # this site Gating a caller's pull requests ¶ A caller that wants one required status check for its branch protection adds the CI gate of hf-general-ci-tools ( ru-ci-gate.yml ) as the last job, and requires only the gate's check: jobs : build : uses : hardfoc/hf-espidf-ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-build.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read pull-requests : write with : project_dir : examples/esp32 ci-gate : name : CI gate needs : [ build ] if : always() uses : hardfoc/hf-general-ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-ci-gate.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read with : needs_json : ${{ toJSON(needs) }} The gate fails when a job it waits for failed or was cancelled. if: always() makes it run, and report, even then. See ru-ci-gate .

docs.text: Versioning ¶ How the workflows are versioned, which ref to pin, what counts as breaking and how a release is cut. Many repositories call these reusable workflows. When all of them used @main , one bad commit here broke every one of them at once. Versioning exists so that does not happen again. Scheme ¶ Release tags are immutable semver tags: v1.0.0 , v1.1.0 , v1.1.1 , and so on. The moving major tag ( v1 ) always points at the newest v1.x.y release. Callers pin the major tag : uses : hardfoc/hf-espidf-ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-build.yml@v1 They receive fixes and new optional inputs automatically, never a breaking change. A caller that needs to be fully reproducible can pin an exact tag ( @v1.2.0 ) or a commit SHA. - @main is the development line. Its first users are the self-tests in this repository. What is breaking ¶ Anything that can make an existing, correct caller fail: Change Why it breaks A reusable workflow removed or renamed uses: no longer resolves An input removed Callers that pass it get startup_failure An input's type changed Callers that pass the old type get startup_failure An input or secret made required, or a new required one added Callers that do not pass it get startup_failure An output removed Callers that read it get empty values A job needs a permission it did not need before Callers that grant the old set get startup_failure A breaking change needs a major bump ( v1 → v2 ). It is listed under ### Breaking in the Unreleased section of the changelog . On pull requests, the self-CI ( .github/scripts/check_contract.py ) compares each ru-*.yml with the base branch. It fails if it finds one of these changes and that heading is missing. Everything else is a minor release (new workflow, new optional input, new output) or a patch release (bug fix, action bump, documentation). Deprecating instead of removing ¶ To retire an input within a major: Keep declaring it, so callers that pass it keep starting. Prefix its description with Deprecated: and say what replaces it. Ignore it, or map it onto the replacement. When it is set, emit a ::warning:: that names the replacement. List it under ### Deprecated in the changelog. Remove it in the next major, and list the removal under ### Breaking . Cutting a release (maintainers) ¶ Releases of this repository are cut by hand: a merge to main does not tag anything, so @v1 callers get a fix when a maintainer tags it. (hf-general-ci-tools releases a patch automatically on every push to main ; this repository's release.yml runs on tags only.) Move the Unreleased entries in CHANGELOG.md under a new ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD heading, and merge that to main . Tag the merge commit and push the tag: git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "v1.0.0" git push origin v1.0.0 release.yml then creates the GitHub Release with generated notes. If the tag is the highest v1.*.* release, it also force-updates v1 to the same commit. A pre-release tag ( v1.1.0-rc.1 ) gets a pre-release and leaves v1 alone. A patch to an older minor does not move v1 backwards. The release workflow pushes v1 with the workflow token. If a tag ruleset protects v* , allow GitHub Actions to update it, or move the tag by hand. Re-runs use the old revision ¶ Re-run failed jobs reruns the workflow at the revision the original run resolved, including the revision of each reusable workflow. After a fix lands here, or after v1 moves, start a new run instead: push a commit, use Run workflow , or close and reopen the pull request. Keeping callers current ¶ Callers pinned to @v1 need nothing more for minor and patch releases. For majors, and for callers that pin exact tags or SHAs, Dependabot with package-ecosystem: github-actions proposes the update, because it also tracks uses: references to reusable workflows. Inside this repository ¶ The workflows in this repository pin third-party actions to full commit SHAs with a # vX.Y.Z comment. Dependabot ( .github/dependabot.yml ) keeps both current. A reusable workflow cannot refer to an action in its own repository at the caller's ref. A uses: hardfoc/hf-espidf-ci-tools/.github/actions/...@main inside ru-build.yml would run main's copy even for callers pinned to @v1 . ru-build.yml therefore inlines the ensure-tools-directory script, and the self-CI checks that the two copies match.
docs.title: Versioning

The build job runs once per matrix entry inside the espressif/idf Docker image and uploads the build folder as a fw-* artifact. On pull requests the size-report job comments a size table. When the caller pushes a version tag, ru-release-with-artifacts downloads the fw-* artifacts built for that commit and attaches them to a GitHub Release. Job names are read from the workflow files.
